title: Length Unit Converter: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Length Unit Converter: Metres, feet, inches, miles and more. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Metres, feet, inches, miles and more. Enter your value and from unit and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert between metric and imperial length units in one step — every result is shown at once so you don't need to convert twice. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Conversion tools include [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter), [Weight Converter](/weight-converter) and [Area Converter](/area-converter). People also look for this tool as "unit converter", "length converter", "cm to inches".

## How to use the Length Unit Converter

Start by entering your value, then choosing your from unit from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your value.
2. Choose your from unit from the list.
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Value in metres × (1 ÷ target unit in metres). 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 ft = 0.3048 m, 1 mi = 1.609344 km.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 100 cm = 1 m = 39.37 in = 3.28 ft. Try the same figures in the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Value: 100, From unit: Centimetres), the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) returns mm: 1,000, cm: 100, m: 1, km: 0.001, in: 39.370079, ft: 3.28084, yd: 1.093613, mi: 0.000621. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- 1 inch is exactly 2.54 cm by definition.
- For height, 5 ft 10 in = 177.8 cm.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many cm in a foot?

30.48 cm. Try it with your own numbers in the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many km in a mile?

1.609344 km. Try it with your own numbers in the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Length Unit Converter use?

Value in metres × (1 ÷ target unit in metres). 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 ft = 0.3048 m, 1 mi = 1.609344 km. You can see it in action in the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Length Unit Converter?

Just Value and From unit. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
